prompt: Ana builds `hits` with a plain `go build` on a machine where `CGO_ENABLED` is 1, yet `ldd hits` says `not a dynamic executable`. Why?
hint: Look at what `go list -deps . | grep -x runtime/cgo` answered.

choices.text: Go never links anything dynamically when it builds for Linux
choices.why: Section 02's `probe` came out `dynamically linked` from the same compiler, because `os/user` used cgo.

choices.text: Nothing it imports has a C implementation
choices.why: Right. `grep` found no `runtime/cgo` among the dependencies and exited 1, so the switch had nothing to switch on.

choices.text: `ldd` only reads binaries built with `CGO_ENABLED=0`
choices.why: `ldd` read `probe` and listed `libc.so.6` and the loader. It reads any ELF file and reports what it would load.

choices.text: `-trimpath` strips the dynamic section out of the file
choices.why: This build used no flags at all. `-trimpath` rewrites recorded file paths and has nothing to do with linking.

prompt: `ldd probe` listed `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`. What is that file's job?
hint: It is not the C library itself; that was the line above it.

choices.text: The dynamic loader, which joins `libc.so.6` to the program
choices.why: Right. A dynamically linked binary names its loader, and the kernel runs the loader, which finds the libraries and links them in.

choices.text: It is the Go runtime, which every Go program on the machine shares
choices.why: The Go runtime is inside every Go binary; `hits` is static and still has one. Nothing Go-specific is shared.

choices.text: It is a page of kernel code mapped into every process, with no file
choices.why: That is `linux-vdso.so.1`, which is not a file at all. The loader is a real file on disk.

choices.text: It is the cgo compiler, which turns the C parts into code at start-up
choices.why: cgo runs at build time, through `gcc`. Nothing compiles anything when `probe` starts.

prompt: Built with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `probe` is `statically linked` and still prints Ana's account, São Paulo's time and 127 authorities. What does that tell you about the image it will go into?
hint: Static removed one kind of dependency. What kind is left?

choices.text: Nothing: a static binary carries everything it needs
choices.why: The answers came from `/etc/passwd`, `/usr/share/zoneinfo` and the certificate bundle of this machine. Section 04 runs the same binary where those files are missing, and all three answers fail.

choices.text: The image must provide glibc, because `os/user` calls it
choices.why: With cgo off `os/user` reads `/etc/passwd` itself; `ldd` said `not a dynamic executable`.

choices.text: It needs no C library, but it still reads data files that the image has to contain
choices.why: Right. `CGO_ENABLED=0` removed the C library and the loader. The user database, the zone rules and the certificates are data, read at run time from whatever filesystem the program sees.

choices.text: It will only run on Ubuntu 24.04
choices.why: Nothing in a static Linux binary is tied to a distribution. Section 04 runs it on Debian's distroless files and it answers.

prompt: The `Containerfile` has two `FROM` lines. What ends up in `hits:1`?
hint: Only one stage becomes the image.

choices.text: Both stages, merged into one filesystem
choices.why: Then the image would weigh more than the 912 MB of `golang`. It is 5.84 MB.

choices.text: The distroless base and the one file `COPY --from=build` named
choices.why: Right. Only the last stage becomes the image, and the only thing it takes from the first is `/src/hits`.

choices.text: The Go toolchain and the source, so that the program rebuilds itself on start
choices.why: The toolchain stays in the build stage. `podman history` shows the binary layer and the base's twelve, nothing else.

choices.text: The first stage, because it is named
choices.why: The name `build` is only a handle for `COPY --from`. Being named does not make a stage ship.

prompt: Put the lines of section 03's `Containerfile` in the order the file has them.
hint: One stage builds, the next ships.

prompt: `~/ship/.containerignore` reads `*`, `!go.mod`, `!*.go`, `!internal/`. Which of these files reach the build stage through `COPY . .`? Choose every one that does.
hint: `*` shuts everything out; each `!` lets one pattern back, matched from the top of the context.

choices.text: `go.mod`
choices.why: Named by `!go.mod`.

choices.text: `internal/tally/tally.go`
choices.why: `!internal/` lets the directory back with everything under it.

choices.text: `main_test.go`
choices.why: It is a `.go` file at the top of the context, so `!*.go` matches it. Harmless, and a reason to read what a pattern matches before trusting it.

choices.text: `access.log`
choices.why: Nothing lets it back after `*`, which is the point: 20,000 lines the build does not need.

choices.text: `cosign.key`
choices.why: Shut out by `*`. A private key in a build context is how keys end up published inside images.

choices.text: `tools/genlog/main.go`
choices.why: `*.go` matches names at the top only, and nothing names `tools/`. The listing of `/src` in the build stage had no `tools` directory.

prompt: `private.log` has mode 600 and belongs to Ana. Mounted with `-v "$PWD/private.log:/data/access.log:ro"`, `hits:1` answers `permission denied`. Why?
hint: Who is the process inside, seen from outside?

choices.text: `:ro` forbids reading the file as well as writing it
choices.why: The same `:ro` mount of `access.log`, mode 644, was read without trouble.

choices.text: Distroless has no `open` system call for the program to use
choices.why: System calls belong to the kernel, which every container shares; `hits` opened `access.log` the same way.

choices.text: User 65532 maps to an id that is not Ana
choices.why: Right. Rootless Podman maps container users onto ids set aside for Ana; 65532 lands on one of them, which has no permission on a file only Ana may read.

choices.text: Podman refuses to mount files outside the build context
choices.why: `podman run -v` takes any path the user can reach; the context matters only to `podman build`.

prompt: Right after that failure, `podman run --rm --network=none -i hits:1 top -n 1 < private.log` prints `/login 2576`. Why does this way work?
hint: Who opens the file in each case?

choices.text: `-i` makes the container run as root, which reads any file
choices.why: `-i` only keeps standard input open. The user is still 65532, from the image's configuration.

choices.text: Ana's shell opens the file and sends it down standard input
choices.why: Right. The `<` belongs to the shell, which runs as Ana, and lesson 1's `hits` reads standard input when it is given no file.

choices.text: Without a mount, Podman copies the file into the image before starting it
choices.why: Nothing is copied into the image; it stays 5.84 MB. The bytes flow through a pipe while the container runs.

choices.text: `top` needs fewer permissions to run than `count` does
choices.why: Permissions belong to files and users, not to subcommands. `count` on standard input would work too.

prompt: Match each failure to the file whose absence caused it.
hint: Three came from `probe` on scratch, one from a dynamic `probe` on distroless.

pairs.left: `user: Current requires cgo or $USER set in environment`

prompt: On scratch, `x509.SystemCertPool` returned an empty pool and a `nil` error. Why is that the most dangerous of the three failures?
hint: What would a real program do next?

choices.text: It crashes the program with a panic during start-up, before `main` runs
choices.why: Nothing crashed: `probe` printed `0 authorities` and exited normally.

choices.text: No error is returned, so the program fails later, elsewhere
choices.why: Right. With no error to check, the failure surfaces later and somewhere else, as a certificate the client cannot verify.

choices.text: It turns certificate checking off for every connection the program makes
choices.why: An empty pool trusts nobody; every server certificate fails the check. It is the opposite of disabled.

choices.text: It makes the image larger
choices.why: The scratch image was the smaller one, 4.52 MB against 7.71 MB.

prompt: `probe`, linked against the C library and copied onto Google's base image for static binaries, fails with `exec /probe: no such file or directory`, though `/probe` is in the image. What fixes it?
hint: Which file is really missing, and which image has it?

choices.text: Copying the binary to `/bin/probe` instead, which is where the kernel looks for programs
choices.why: The kernel found `/probe`; it was the loader the binary asks for that it could not find. Moving the binary changes nothing.

choices.text: Running it as root with `--user 0`
choices.why: A missing file is missing for every user. Root changes permissions, not what exists.

choices.text: Build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, or use `distroless/base-debian12`
choices.why: Right. The static build needs no loader at all; the `base` image is the one meant for programs that really need the C library.

choices.text: Adding `--network=host`
choices.why: No network is involved in starting a process. The message is about a file.

prompt: Why does the pinned `Containerfile` write `static-debian12:nonroot@sha256:afa5c872…` rather than the tag alone?
hint: What can change behind a tag, and what can change behind a digest?

choices.text: It makes the pull faster, because Podman skips asking the registry
choices.why: The build in section 04 pulled nothing either way: both bases were already on the machine.

choices.text: A tag gets moved; a digest names those bytes forever
choices.why: Right. The tag stays for people to read; the digest decides, and moving to a newer base becomes an edit somebody reviews.

choices.text: Podman refuses a tag without a digest
choices.why: Section 03 built from tags alone without complaint.

choices.text: It selects the `amd64` image, so an ARM server gets an error
choices.why: `afa5c872…` is the index; it names five images, one per processor, and each machine picks its own.

prompt: To make `time.LoadLocation` work on a scratch image without copying `/usr/share/zoneinfo`, build with `go build -tags ___`, which embeds the zone rules through `time/tzdata`.
hint: It added 410,584 bytes to `probe`.

prompt: After `printf x >> hits-linux-arm64`, Ana reruns the same `go build -o dist/hits-linux-arm64` and `sha256sum -c` still says `FAILED`. Why?
hint: What does `go build` look at before writing an output that already exists?

choices.text: The build cache handed back a corrupted object for the arm64 target
choices.why: The cache was fine: deleting the file and building again produced the right hash from the same cache.

choices.text: `sha256sum` caches its results per file name between runs
choices.why: `sha256sum` hashes the file every time it runs; it keeps nothing between runs.

choices.text: Cross builds for `arm64` are never reproducible from one run to the next
choices.why: The arm64 hash matched `SHA256SUMS` as soon as the file was rebuilt from nothing.

choices.text: `go build` saw a current build ID in the file and kept it
choices.why: Right. The extra byte went on the end and did not touch the build ID, so the go command thought the output was up to date. `rm` first forces a real write.

prompt: `hits` built without flags in `~/ship` and in `~/ship-copy` gives two different SHA-256 hashes; with `-trimpath` the hashes are equal. What differed?
hint: The source was the same.

choices.text: The directory, recorded in the binary
choices.why: Right. Without `-trimpath`, file names like `/home/ana/ship/main.go` go into the binary for stack traces; with it, module paths replace them.

choices.text: The time of the build, which Go stamps into every binary
choices.why: Go writes no build time; that is why the two `-trimpath` builds, made at different moments, came out identical.

choices.text: A random seed the linker draws for each build
choices.why: A random seed would make the `-trimpath` builds differ too, and they did not.

choices.text: The version control information of each directory
choices.why: Neither directory is a git repository, so neither binary recorded any.

prompt: A release page lists the binaries and their `SHA256SUMS`. What does adding a cosign signature of `SHA256SUMS` protect against that the checksums alone do not?
hint: Who is able to change each of the files on that page?

choices.text: A download cut short by a bad connection
choices.why: `sha256sum -c` already catches that: one byte different was enough to print `FAILED`.

choices.text: Somebody who replaces a binary and rewrites its line in `SHA256SUMS` to match
choices.why: Right. Whoever can change the page can change both files; nobody without `cosign.key` can make a signature that verifies over the rewritten list.

choices.text: A binary built for the wrong processor
choices.why: A signature vouches for bytes, not for what they run on; `file` answers that question.

choices.text: A bug in `hits` itself
choices.why: A signature says who stands behind the file. A signed program with a bug still has the bug.

prompt: Ana's `cosign verify-blob` needs `--insecure-ignore-tlog`. What is the flag telling cosign?
hint: Look at `no-tlog.json` and at what `sign-blob` was told to use.

choices.text: To skip checking the signature
choices.why: The signature was checked: a forged `SHA256SUMS` failed with `invalid signature` under the same flag.

choices.text: To trust any public key it finds, including one inside the bundle
choices.why: Only `--key cosign.pub` was trusted. A different key would not verify this bundle.

choices.text: Not to expect a Rekor entry, which this signature never got
choices.why: Right. The empty signing configuration named no log, so there is none to check; the warning says what that costs: nobody else can see when the key signed.

choices.text: To work without network access
choices.why: The network is what the warning on `sign-blob` was about. This flag concerns the log entry, which exists or not regardless of the network.

prompt: Put a signed release of `hits` in order, from the build to the user's last check.
hint: The publisher acts first; the person downloading checks the signature before the checksums.
items: build each target with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w"`
publish the binaries, `SHA256SUMS`, the bundle and `cosign.pub`
the user runs `cosign verify-blob --key cosign.pub` on `SHA256SUMS`

prompt: A colleague ships a `CGO_ENABLED=0` Go service that calls an HTTPS API, in an image `FROM scratch`. It starts, and every request fails with a certificate signed by an unknown authority. What is the smallest correct fix?
hint: Which of `probe`'s three questions is this?

choices.text: Rebuild with `CGO_ENABLED=1` so the C library supplies the certificates
choices.why: The C library holds no certificates, and on scratch a cgo binary would not even start: there is no loader.

choices.text: Run the container with `--user 0`
choices.why: Root does not create files that are not there; the pool stays empty.

choices.text: Put a CA bundle in the image, by copying one from the build stage or by moving to `distroless/static`
choices.why: Right. The program found no bundle, so it trusts nobody. Either copy `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` in or use the base that carries Debian's, kept current by somebody else.

choices.text: Build with `-tags timetzdata`
choices.why: That embeds the zone rules, the second of `probe`'s questions. Certificates are the third.

prompt: `podman images` showed `probe:distroless` at 7.71 MB and `probe:scratch` at 4.52 MB, the same binary on two bases. How many MB is the distroless base?
hint: The binary is in both; subtract.
